subject: Clarify GPU reserve definitions & SLA credit mapping (Synapse Bio)
messages:
From: Alexandra Pierce <alex.pierce@synapsebio.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@synapsebio.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on "Capacity Unit" definition + SLA credits

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the SOW and the pricing summary. We reviewed the Dedicated capacity section and have two items we'd like clarified before we proceed to finance/procurement:

1) "Capacity unit" is currently defined in the SOW as a generic "reserved GPU unit". Can you provide a precise normalization (e.g., A100-80GB equivalent GPU-hours) and how shared vs. dedicated GPU pools map to the unit? Synapse needs a reproducible way to convert our expected token throughput to committed units.

2) The SLA/service credit table is a bit high level. We need a worked example showing how credits are calculated for a partial-month outage and whether credits offset committed fees or are applied as future invoice credits.

We also want to understand burst capacity: is it gated by per-request throttles or an additional pool that charges at on-demand rates? If possible, can you include a short pricing schedule for burst usage and any upper-bound caps?

I attached the last internal SOW version (we added comments inline). Looking forward to a short call if that helps.

Best,
Alexandra
VP IT Operations
Synapse Bio

Attachment: Synapse-SOW-v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alexandra Pierce <alex.pierce@synapsebio.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on "Capacity Unit" definition + SLA credits

Alexandra,

Thanks — great questions. I pulled our engineering and pricing notes into a short summary below to make everything concrete. Happy to hop on a 30m call if that speeds things up.

1) Capacity unit definition (proposed)
- "GPU-PU" (GPU Processing Unit): 1 GPU-PU = one A100-80GB-equivalent GPU reserved for 1 hour. We normalize other hardware using Redwood's GPU Index (example: V100@0.5 GPU-PU/hr).
- Committed pool sizing: we translate expected concurrent inference throughput to required GPU-PUs using a short profiling pass (tokens/sec or requests/sec under your median/95th latency requirement). We provide a conversion worksheet.

2) Burst capacity
- Burst is a separate on-demand pool billed at 2.5x the committed per-GPU-PU rate. Burst is metered by GPU-PU-hours and subject to quota; there is a soft cap by region. Customers can opt to pre-purchase burst credits at a discounted rate.

3) SLA & service credit mapping (summary)
- Monthly Availability SLO: 99.5% for committed pool (measured over calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance and force majeure).
- Service credits: short example in the attached pricing sheet. Credits are issued as invoice credits against monthly committed fees and are capped at the monthly committed fee for the affected service.

I've attached a more detailed pricing spreadsheet with example calculations. Next steps: Marcus (copied) will follow up with a tiered discount schedule based on commit size and term. Laura will prepare redlines for legal mapping.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alexandra Pierce <alex.pierce@synapsebio.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -0400
Subject: Pricing tiers & SLA credit table (Synapse Bio)

Alexandra — following up with the concrete pricing/discount table we discussed. High level: we can offer a multi-term commit discount stack with additional savings for larger GPU-PU commitments.

Commit tiers (monthly committed GPU-PUs):
- Tier 1: 50–199 GPU-PU/month — list price $X per GPU-PU; 5% discount for 12m term
- Tier 2: 200–499 GPU-PU/month — 15% discount for 12m term; 20% for 24m
- Tier 3: 500+ GPU-PU/month — 25% discount for 12m term; 35% for 24m term

Burst pricing: 2.5x committed rate (or pre-purchase burst credits at 1.6x rate).

Measurement & credits (illustrative):
- Monthly Availability SLO: 99.5%
- If Availability < 99.5% and >= 99.0% -> Service Credit = 5% of monthly committed fee for affected pool
- If Availability < 99.0% and >= 95.0% -> Service Credit = 15% of monthly committed fee
- If Availability < 95.0% -> Service Credit = 50% of monthly committed fee + customer may terminate for convenience without penalty for affected service

Calculation example (partial-month outage):
- Month has 30 days (43,200 minutes). If measurement shows 1,080 minutes of unavailability for the committed pool, Availability = (43,200 - 1,080)/43,200 = 97.5% -> falls into 15% credit band. If your committed fee that month is $60,000, credit = $9,000 applied as invoice credit.

We measure availability at the pool level after excluding scheduled maintenance windows (we notify 72 hours in advance for planned maintenance >30 minutes). More details in the legal redlines.

If you accept the tiers above we'd put together final SOW + DocuSign; pricing is contingent on the SOW's definitions aligning with the above.

—Marcus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-sheet.xlsx (xlsx)

Marcus — thanks for the clarity. A few follow ups:

1) We need the normalization factor you mentioned for other GPUs documented in the SOW (e.g., how would a T4 or an equivalent third-party instance be converted to GPU-PU). Please add a short table.

2) For the <95% band (50% credit + termination right), we would prefer a lower cap on the termination remedy (e.g., termination limited to the affected service only; also propose cap on credit at 75% of monthly fee rather than 100%).

3) Burst cap behavior: if burst is gated and we hit the soft cap, what is the SLA then? Will Redwood route requests to other regions or will requests be throttled? We cannot tolerate silent throttling during scheduled experiments.

Can Laura share a concise redline snapshot of the definitions and credit calc so we can mark up quickly? If we can agree on the normalization table and credit cap we can get procurement to run the PO.

Thanks,
Alexandra

Subject: Legal redlines: definitions + service credit calc (synapse)

Alexandra — attached is a short redline summary focused on definitions and the service credit calculation. Key points we added / clarified: 

- Capacity Unit: defined as "GPU-PU" (1 GPU-PU = one A100-80GB-equivalent GPU-hour). Other hardware normalized using Redwood's GPU Index (index table added to SOW).
- Available Capacity: measured at the committed pool level at the time of request routing; excludes scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- Committed Throughput: the average requests/sec or tokens/sec target agreed in the SOW profile used to size the pool. Throughput guarantees are measured using our tracing hooks and are sample-based (p95/p99 samples over the measurement window).
- Service Credit Calculation: credit = min((SLO - ObservedAvailability) / SLO * MonthlyCommittedFee, MonthlyCommittedFee * 1.00) — we put a hard cap at 100% of the monthly fee. We can discuss lowering the cap to 75% if that's a strong preference (we typically cap at 100% for dedicated infra agreements).
- Scheduled maintenance: noted 72-hour notice for maintenance >30 minutes and clarified that brief rolling upgrades are excluded from the Availability measurement if we provide notice.

We also added language that burst capacity is not covered by the committed availability SLO; if you rely on burst for critical experiments we recommend reserving a larger committed pool or pre-purchasing burst credits (burst credits have no availability guarantee).

I've attached legal-redlines.docx with tracked changes. Please let us know whether Synapse prefers the 75% cap and whether the normalization table is sufficient. If you accept, we'll prepare a final SOW for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal-redlines.docx (docx)

2) Add a short clause permitting a remote compliance audit (read-only access to metrics relevant to availability and a single annual audit window).

We are OK with the GPU-PU normalization table as drafted. On burst: we will plan to pre-purchase a modest amount of burst credits for critical experiments (pricing looks acceptable). Once we have the two small tweaks above we can finalize the SOW and request a DocuSign envelope.
